speed_metrics.decode_gap_retrospective: In R60's env.json I wrote 'Decode has an irreducible ~9% gap from R44 baseline... the Claude Code co-tenants cannot be cleaned up while this cron is active.' R61 DISPROVES that conclusion. With ~2 hours of additional system page-out since R60, the 4K decode path recovered fully (31.6 -> 35.1) and now MATCHES/BEATS R44. The gap WAS reducible — it just required more idle time than R60 had. Analyst self-correction.

memory.swap_peak_progression: R44/R47/R48: 0.0, R58: 12.9 breach, R59: 5.48, R60: 4.41, R61: 0.75. Trending toward clean-box zero without user intervention between R60 and R61.

profiler.cpu_scheduling_fraction_progression: R60: 0.9919, R61: 0.9932. Cleanest run in session by this metric.

swap_io_mb_per_s.max_anomaly_note: 547.8 MB/s max. Much more believable than R59's 2678 or R60's 2524 — closer to the M4 Pro's ~430 MB/s advertised ceiling. Suggests the profiler sampler artifact is pressure-dependent: it only spikes to impossible values when the sampler itself is briefly paged out mid-interval. A cleaner run produces more believable max readings.
